domain: reunion dinner at a dim sum restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a dim sum reunion dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and logistics. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, my family is getting together for a reunion dinner this Saturday at a dim sum place. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Five of us: me, Uncle Hao, Auntie Mei, cousin Derek, and Grandma
Uncle Hao had a gout flare-up last month and his doctor told him to watch his diet carefully
Cousin Derek ate peanuts at a party once and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Should I book a table for 5 or get a private room?

Uncle Hao just called — his flight got moved up so he has to leave for the airport right after he drops Grandma off. He won't be staying for dinner. But he said he really wants me to pack him a box of his favorites to take on the plane
Auntie Mei is bringing her daughter Sophie, she's 4. Sophie was in the hospital last year because she ate shrimp and broke out in hives everywhere, it was really scary
Grandma just got new dentures fitted last week, she told me she can only do really soft foods right now
Auntie Mei just texted — she has to run to a work emergency after dropping Sophie off, so she'll leave around noon. Sophie will stay with us though, Grandma will watch her
Should we get tea or do they have other drinks? Grandma loves chrysanthemum tea
OK so I'm looking at the menu. How about these: har gow (shrimp dumplings), char siu bao (BBQ pork buns), turnip cake, chicken feet, and peanut sesame balls. Any issues?

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a family reunion dim sum dinner. You will introduce 5 family members with various dietary issues, then the group will change: Uncle Hao leaves but wants takeaway packed, Auntie Mei's young daughter Sophie joins with a shrimp allergy, Grandma gets a new constraint (soft foods only), and Auntie Mei leaves but Sophie stays. At the end you will list 5 specific dim sum dishes and ask if there are any issues. You must NEVER hint at which dishes are problematic — just list them and ask.

You are a calm, cooperative family organizer. You always refer to family members by name in third person (e.g. 'Uncle Hao just called...', 'Auntie Mei texted me...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal family coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family updates

ground_truth.answer: Har gow (shrimp dumplings): problematic for Sophie who has a shrimp allergy and is present at the table; also should not be packed for Uncle Hao's takeaway since shrimp is high-purine and he has gout. Char siu bao (BBQ pork buns): fine for everyone at the table and fine for Uncle Hao's takeaway. Turnip cake: fine for everyone at the table and fine for Uncle Hao's takeaway (soft, no allergens, low-purine). Chicken feet: problematic for Grandma because they are tough and chewy, not suitable for someone with new dentures who can only eat soft foods; also should not be packed for Uncle Hao since chicken feet are moderately high in purines. Peanut sesame balls: problematic for cousin Derek who has a severe peanut allergy. Auntie Mei left but has no dietary constraints that matter — her departure changes nothing. Sophie stays at the table even though Auntie Mei left, so Sophie's shrimp allergy remains active for all shared dishes.

ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking with scope changes across a dim sum reunion dinner. The agent must track: (1) Uncle Hao has gout → must avoid high-purine foods like shrimp and organ meats (inferential chain from 'gout flare-up' + 'doctor told him to watch diet'), (2) Uncle Hao EXITS the dinner but wants takeaway packed → his gout constraint applies ONLY to the takeaway box, not to what others eat at the table, (3) Sophie (age 4) JOINS late with a shrimp allergy, (4) Grandma gets a NEW constraint mid-conversation (new dentures → soft foods only), (5) Auntie Mei EXITS but Sophie STAYS — the child's shrimp allergy remains active for shared table food even though the parent left. At probe time with 5 dishes: har gow fails for Sophie at the table (shrimp) AND for Uncle Hao's takeaway (high-purine shrimp); chicken feet fail for Grandma (not soft); peanut sesame balls fail for Derek (peanut allergy); char siu bao and turnip cake are fine for everyone present. The over-generalization trap is Derek's peanut allergy — it is specifically peanuts, not all nuts or sesame.

mechanism: Entity EXIT with scope change: person leaves but wants something packed/saved
